circumstances: The researcher performs the end-to-end manuscript read-through planned on Day 12. The main discovery is a wording mismatch in the methods section: an older draft describes the shifted evaluation set more broadly than the configuration actually used. The researcher checks the frozen configuration and experiment logs, confirms the experiments themselves used the intended narrower shift, and corrects the manuscript wording. A collaborator leaves comments questioning whether one result should be framed as a main finding or a limitation. The researcher drafts a cautious response and revises the discussion. The day is lighter than the preceding workdays, with a long offline period and some unrelated browsing.

key_observations: The end-to-end read-through exposed a genuine methods-to-configuration wording mismatch that had survived into the assembled draft.
The underlying experiments were consistent with the frozen configuration, so the issue was corrected at the manuscript level rather than by rerunning the experiments.
Collaborator feedback pushed the generalization claim toward a narrower and more defensible interpretation.
The manuscript now has a clearer evidence boundary, although several consistency checks remain before it is ready for a broader review.
The replication study remained untouched and appropriately parked.
